Section 03  —  Product Story

The Willow tree moves differently from other trees. Its branches do not stand rigid against the wind. They bend, they drape, they trail — and in that movement there is a particular kind of beauty. Not the beauty of resistance, but the beauty of adaptation. Of finding grace in circumstances that require flexibility rather than force.

Willow Wrap takes its name from that quality. Named after the same tree that gives the Willow Support bra its name, the scarf represents a consistent idea within the Nuvanaah family: that strength does not have to be rigid, that support does not have to be heavy, and that comfort and beauty are not opposing forces.

Head scarves have a long history across cultures as objects of beauty, identity, and personal expression. They are also, for women navigating treatment-related hair loss, deeply practical objects — one of the simplest and most accessible forms of coverage available. Willow Wrap was designed to honour both of those realities. To be genuinely useful as a coverage solution while being genuinely beautiful as a personal object.

The bamboo plant-fiber fabric was chosen because bamboo has its own relationship with flexibility and resilience. It grows faster than almost any other plant, it bends in wind and returns upright, and the fibers it produces are among the softest available in natural textiles. Wrapping the head in bamboo plant-fiber fabric is, in the most literal sense, wrapping it in something from nature that is both gentle and strong.

The three prints — Wildflower Garden, Willow Print, and Aparajita Petals — were chosen because coverage during recovery deserves to be beautiful. Not clinical. Not plain. Not an afterthought. A wildflower garden, a flowing willow branch, scattered petals: images of life continuing, growing, blooming. Images that belong in recovery spaces.
Willow Wrap. Inspired by nature. Designed for comfort. Made for every day.

Section 06  —  Materials & Construction
Bamboo Plant-Fiber Fabric

Willow Wrap is made entirely from bamboo plant-fiber fabric. Bamboo fiber is derived from the bamboo plant through a process that extracts the natural cellulose fibers from the plant material and processes them into a soft, fine textile. The resulting fabric has several properties that make it particularly well-suited to a head covering worn directly against the skin.

Softness: Bamboo fibers are finer than cotton fibers, which produces a fabric with a noticeably smoother, softer texture at the surface. This softness is intrinsic to the fiber structure rather than produced by finishing treatments, which means it is maintained through regular washing over the lifespan of the product.

Breathability: The structure of bamboo fiber fabric allows air to pass through it freely, which prevents heat from being trapped between the fabric and the scalp during wear. This is the quality that makes bamboo particularly suitable for head coverings worn for extended periods, particularly in warm environments.

Lightweight: Bamboo fabric is lighter than equivalent cotton fabric of the same thickness, which contributes to the overall sensation of wearing very little rather than being conscious of something sitting on the head.

Colorfastness: The prints on Willow Wrap are applied to the bamboo fabric in a process that produces consistent, fade-resistant colour through the regular washing and wearing cycle recommended for the product.
Print Application

The three prints — Wildflower Garden, Willow Print, and Aparajita Petals — are printed at the fabric level rather than applied as a surface coating. This means the colour and pattern are integrated into the fabric rather than sitting on top of it, which prevents peeling, cracking, or significant fading through washing. The prints are clear and consistent across the full length of the scarf.
Dimensions and Drape

Section 09  —  How To Use
Willow Wrap can be worn in several different ways depending on the level of coverage needed and the look you want to achieve. Below are three of the most practical and commonly used methods.
Classic Tied Wrap — Full Coverage
Fold the scarf lengthwise to your preferred width — a wider fold for more coverage, a narrower fold for a more fitted look.
Place the center of the scarf at the back of the head, at the nape of the neck.
Bring both ends forward, crossing them over the top of the head.
Take the ends to the back and tie in a secure knot or bow at the nape.
Adjust the fabric at the front to sit at a comfortable position at the forehead. The folded edge can be positioned to show or to tuck under depending on preference.
Front Knot Style — Relaxed and Personal
Place the center of the scarf at the back of the head.
Bring both ends forward to the front.
Tie the ends together in a knot or bow at the front of the head, slightly off-center.
Adjust the scarf so it sits evenly across the head. The tied knot becomes part of the visual design of the look.
Soft Drape — Informal and Comfortable
Drape the scarf over the head without folding, letting it fall naturally at the sides.
Gather the ends loosely at the back or side of the neck and secure with a light knot or tuck the ends in.
Adjust the front of the scarf so it sits comfortably at the hairline or forehead position you prefer.

These are starting points rather than fixed methods. The softness and drape of bamboo plant-fiber fabric means Willow Wrap settles naturally into most positions without needing to be pinned or held in place.
Section 10  —  Care Instructions
Washing
Willow Wrap can be hand washed or machine washed on a gentle cycle. Both methods are appropriate for bamboo plant-fiber fabric when the following guidelines are observed.
Hand Washing (Recommended)
Fill a clean basin with cool to lukewarm water.
Add a small amount of mild detergent.
Submerge the scarf and gently agitate for one to two minutes.
Rinse thoroughly in cool water until no detergent remains.
Gently press excess water from the fabric without wringing or twisting.
Lay flat on a clean dry towel or hang in a well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight to dry.
Machine Washing
Use a gentle or delicate cycle with cool water and mild detergent. Place the scarf inside a mesh laundry bag to protect the fabric and prevent tangling. Do not tumble dry.
Storage

Willow Wrap can be folded and stored in a clean drawer or laid flat in a breathable bag. Avoid storing in direct sunlight for extended periods, which can affect the colour and quality of the fabric over time. The scarf can be gently rolled rather than folded to prevent persistent crease lines if stored for longer periods.
What Not to Do
Do not bleach
Do not tumble dry
Do not iron on high heat — if ironing is needed, use a low heat setting with a cloth between the iron and the fabric
Do not wring or twist when wet
Do not dry in direct sunlight for extended periods
Lifespan and Care

Bamboo plant-fiber fabric maintains its softness through regular washing better than many natural textiles. The prints are colourfast through the recommended care process. With proper washing and storage, Willow Wrap is designed to remain as soft, as vibrant, and as comfortable as it was when new across many months of regular use.

FlowSleeve is a lymphedema compression sleeve designed to provide gentle, consistent arm compression and everyday support for individuals managing arm swelling, heaviness, or discomfort following breast cancer treatment and recovery. Thoughtfully constructed with soft, breathable compression fabric and an adjustable shoulder holding belt, FlowSleeve is built for the reality of daily life — for work, travel, rest, and movement — not just for clinical settings.

The compression sleeve provides consistent gentle pressure along the arm, which may help support lymphatic circulation and manage the swelling and discomfort associated with lymphedema. The adjustable shoulder holding belt is a design detail that addresses one of the most common practical frustrations with compression sleeves: slipping. The belt keeps the sleeve in position throughout the day, reducing the need for constant readjustment and giving the wearer greater confidence in movement.

FlowSleeve is available in two options: an Indian version at ₹ 1,575 and an imported version at ₹ 2,840. Both provide the same core function of gentle compression with a holding belt. The choice between them allows for flexibility based on personal preference and budget.

The fabric is soft and skin-friendly, selected for comfort against skin that may be sensitive during recovery. It is breathable enough for extended daily wear, including in warm conditions, and constructed to move with the arm rather than restricting natural range of motion.

FlowSleeve is designed with a simple, clear intention: because healing deserves comfort, because support should feel gentle, and because the experience of managing lymphedema should not add to the difficulty of a period that is already demanding enough.
Section 03  —  Product Story
The name FlowSleeve is built from two simple words that together describe exactly what the product is designed to do.

Flow represents the lymphatic system and the goal of supporting it — the gentle, consistent movement of fluid through the arm that lymphedema disrupts and that compression sleeves are designed to support. It is also a word that speaks to ease, to movement, to the experience of the arm feeling less heavy, less restricted, less constantly present in your awareness. Flow is what lymphedema takes away, in various degrees, and what FlowSleeve is designed to help restore.

Sleeve is simply what it is. A compression sleeve. There is clarity in that directness: this product does not try to be something other than what it is, and it does not dress up a functional medical support garment in language that obscures its purpose. It is a sleeve. A good one, designed with care.

The holding belt came from listening. One of the most consistent pieces of feedback about compression sleeves from people who wear them daily is that they slip. They need to be pulled back up throughout the day. They shift during movement. The constant readjustment is both practically inconvenient and emotionally exhausting — one more thing to manage in a day that is already full of things that need managing.

The adjustable shoulder belt is the design response to that feedback. It keeps the sleeve where it belongs, without elastic digging into the shoulder, without complicated fastening systems, and without requiring attention throughout the day. It is a small engineering decision with a significant impact on the quality of daily life for the person wearing the sleeve.

FlowSleeve was also created with the understanding that managing lymphedema is a long-term reality for many women after breast cancer treatment, not a short-term recovery task. A product designed for that reality needs to be comfortable enough to wear every day, durable enough to last through regular use, and practical enough to integrate into a normal daily routine without friction.
Comfort. Care. Confidence. In every detail of the design.

FlowSleeve’s fabric is soft at the skin contact surface and maintains that softness through regular washing.

Section 09  —  How To Use
Putting On FlowSleeve
Ensure your arm is clean and dry before putting on the sleeve. Lotions or oils can make it difficult to slide the sleeve on and can degrade the fabric over time.
Turn the sleeve inside out to the mid-point and gather the lower half of the sleeve.
Place the gathered lower end of the sleeve at the wrist and begin rolling the sleeve up the arm, smoothing it as you go to eliminate any folds or bunches.
Continue rolling until the sleeve is fully extended up the arm, with the top of the sleeve sitting at the correct position on the upper arm.
Smooth the sleeve along the full length of the arm to ensure it is lying flat with no folds that could create localised pressure points.
Attach the holding belt to the top of the sleeve according to the fitting guide included with your FlowSleeve.

Pass the belt over the shoulder and adjust it using the adjustment mechanism until it feels secure and comfortable. The belt should hold the sleeve in position without digging into the shoulder or feeling tight.
During the Day

Once fitted correctly, FlowSleeve should require minimal attention throughout the day. If the sleeve feels as though it is shifting, check the belt adjustment and tighten slightly if needed. If any area of the arm feels particularly uncomfortable, unusually numb, or develops any skin reaction, remove the sleeve and rest the arm before reassessing.
Removing FlowSleeve
Release the shoulder holding belt first.
Gently roll the sleeve down the arm from the top, maintaining the same smooth rolling motion used when putting it on. Do not pull the sleeve from the wrist end.
Allow the arm to rest without the sleeve for a period before reapplying if needed.
When to Wear

Follow the guidance of your healthcare professional regarding when and for how long to wear your compression sleeve. General guidance for most daily use scenarios involves wearing the sleeve during waking hours and removing it for rest and sleep, but individual recommendations may vary. Always follow the specific guidance provided for your situation.
Section 10  —  Care Instructions

Proper care of a compression sleeve is essential for maintaining its compression performance over time. The elasticity of the fabric degrades more quickly when washed at high temperatures, with harsh detergents, or tumble dried. Following the care instructions below will significantly extend the effective lifespan of your FlowSleeve.
Washing
Hand wash in lukewarm water — not hot — using a mild detergent or specialist compression garment wash.
Gently agitate in the water for one to two minutes. Do not wring, twist, or scrub.
Rinse thoroughly in cool water until no detergent remains.
Press excess water out gently between two clean towels. Do not wring.
Lay flat or hang to air dry in a well-ventilated area away from direct heat sources and direct sunlight.
Ensure the sleeve is completely dry before wearing again.
Washing Frequency

Daily washing is recommended for compression sleeves that are worn every day. Body oils, sweat, and skin products reduce the effectiveness of the compression fabric over time and washing removes these. Daily washing also maintains hygiene in a garment that is in close contact with the skin for extended periods. Having a second sleeve available allows one to be worn while the other is washed and dried overnight.
Storage

Store the sleeve flat or loosely rolled in a clean, dry location. Do not store compressed under other items, which can distort the fabric’s elasticity over time. Store the holding belt separately from the sleeve to prevent the adjustment mechanism from catching on the compression fabric.
What Not to Do
Do not machine wash on a standard cycle — if machine washing is necessary, use a delicate cycle at 30 degrees with the sleeve in a mesh laundry bag
Do not tumble dry — heat degrades the compression fabric’s elasticity
Do not bleach
Do not iron
Do not dry in direct sunlight or near a heat source
Do not use fabric softener, which coats the fibers and reduces breathability and elasticity
Lifespan

With daily wear and proper care, a compression sleeve typically needs to be replaced every four to six months as the compression properties of the fabric gradually diminish with use. Replace FlowSleeve when it no longer feels as firm as it did when new, when it shows significant stretching, or when it no longer stays in position as well as it did even with the holding belt adjusted.

A dedicated diary creates a single location for all of this, which is simpler to manage and easier to refer back to than scattered notes across different devices and notebooks.
A Thoughtful Gift at an Accessible Price

The completeness of the kit and the care evident in its assembly communicate thought and consideration from the person giving it. Many women who receive Nest Carry as a gift describe it as one of the most genuinely useful things they received during their treatment period.
Designed for Every Stage of Recovery

Nest Carry is relevant from the first days after surgery through the full length of recovery. The items within it address needs that arise at different stages — the jars most relevant in early post-surgical care, the therapy ball through the middle stages of recovery as movement is encouraged, and the diary throughout the entire journey. The kit grows with the recovery rather than becoming redundant after the first few weeks.
Section 05  —  Key Benefits
Reducing the Cognitive Load of Recovery

Recovery is demanding in ways that extend well beyond the physical. The mental effort of managing appointments, tracking progress, organising medications and supplies, remembering what to bring to which appointment and what to ask when you get there — these demands accumulate and exhaust. Nest Carry addresses this by reducing the number of organisational decisions involved in daily recovery management. The bag keeps everything together. The diary keeps everything written down. The pen means you always have what you need to write with. None of these are complex solutions. That simplicity is the point.
Supporting Hand and Arm Health Through Gentle Daily Exercise

After breast cancer surgery, particularly surgery involving lymph node removal, maintaining gentle movement in the hand and arm on the treated side is important for lymphatic health, preventing stiffness, and supporting recovery of normal mobility. The smiley therapy ball provides a tool for this that is soft enough for sensitive hands, portable enough to use anywhere, and simple enough to use without instruction. Squeezing it during television, during rest, in waiting rooms — these micro-exercises accumulate into meaningful daily movement support.
Keeping Appointments and Observations in One Place

The recovery diary serves a need that almost every woman in treatment develops: the need for a single, dedicated place to record the information that recovery generates. Appointment dates and times matter because missing them has consequences. Medication details matter because they change. Observations matter because they inform the conversations with healthcare teams that guide treatment decisions. Having a recovery diary means nothing needs to be carried only in memory, on scattered pieces of paper, or across multiple apps. Everything is in one place, in one notebook, carried in the same bag as everything else.
Portable Essentials That Go Everywhere Recovery Goes

The 100 mL jar’s measurement markings make volume tracking straightforward without additional tools.
The Value of Being Prepared

One of the quieter benefits of Nest Carry is simply the feeling of being prepared. Recovery involves uncertainty at many levels, and the ability to exert control over the practical elements of daily life — to know that your diary is in the bag, your therapy ball is in the bag, your jars are in the bag, and the bag is where it always is — provides a small but genuine sense of order and agency during a period when many things feel out of control. That sense of preparedness has value beyond its practical dimensions.
Section 06  —  Materials & Construction

The bag is sized for practical daily carry without being bulky or heavy. Its exterior is finished in a neutral colour suitable for use in all settings, including medical appointments where a more neutral aesthetic is appropriate. The closure is easy to operate with one hand, which matters for women who may be managing with limited arm mobility on the treated side.
Smiley Therapy Ball

The material is gentle against hand skin that may be sensitive following treatment. The ball’s size is calibrated to fit comfortably in most adult hands without requiring a wide grip, making it appropriate for use even when grip strength is reduced or hand mobility is limited.

The smiley design on the ball is a considered detail. The expression on the ball provides a small, consistent moment of lightness during exercises that may otherwise feel like clinical obligations. This is a minor thing, but minor things accumulate in recovery.
50 mL and 100 mL Collection Jars

The 100 mL jar includes measurement markings on the exterior that allow volume to be read accurately without transferring the liquid to a separate measuring container. Both jars have secure screw-top closures that prevent leaking during transport and storage. Recovery Diary

The recovery diary is a notebook of sufficient size and page count for sustained use over the course of recovery. The cover is firm enough to allow writing without a separate hard surface, which makes it practical to use in settings such as waiting rooms where a desk surface may not be available. The pages are lined for organised note-taking.

Section 08  —  How To Use
Setting Up Your Nest Carry
When your Nest Carry arrives, place all components into the sling bag according to your preference for access and organisation.
Keep the diary and pen accessible in an outer pocket or front compartment if available, so they can be reached quickly when needed.
Store the jars in a secure inner compartment where they will not shift during movement.
Keep the therapy ball where it can be reached with one hand without opening the full bag.
Choose a consistent home location for the bag — beside the bed, next to a favourite chair, or in the room where most rest happens — so it is always in the same place and always within reach.
Using the Sling Bag

Adjust the strap to a comfortable length for your height and carrying preference. The bag should sit at a height that allows easy access to the main compartment without bending or reaching. For women with limited shoulder mobility on the treated side, position the bag on the opposite shoulder and adjust the strap so the bag rests comfortably against the opposite hip.
Using the Therapy Ball

Squeeze the ball gently and release, repeating at a pace that feels comfortable. Start with a small number of repetitions and build gradually as comfort and grip strength allow. The ball can be used while seated, during rest, in waiting rooms, or while watching television. There is no minimum or maximum recommended number of repetitions. The goal is gentle, consistent daily movement rather than effort or intensity. Follow the specific guidance of your healthcare team regarding hand and arm exercises if you have received it.
Using the Recovery Diary

Begin the diary by recording your name, the date you started using it, and any key information you want to have easily accessible — healthcare team contacts, medication names, key appointment dates. Then use it daily or as frequently as needed to record appointments, observations, questions for your next consultation, and any personal notes or reflections that feel worth keeping. There is no right or wrong way to use a recovery diary. Use it in whatever way helps you feel organised and in possession of your own recovery story.
Using the Collection Jars

Use the jars as directed by your healthcare team for any liquid collection, measurement, or storage tasks that are part of your recovery management. Rinse and clean the jars after each use. The measurement markings on the 100 mL jar allow volume to be read without transferring liquid to a separate container.

Therapy Ball

Wipe the therapy ball with a clean damp cloth. For deeper cleaning, wash with mild soap and water and allow to dry completely before use. Do not submerge for extended periods. Store in the sling bag when not in use to keep it clean and accessible.
Collection Jars

Wash both jars with mild soap and warm water after each use. Rinse thoroughly and allow to dry completely before storing or reusing. The jars can be hand washed or washed in a dishwasher on a standard cycle. Ensure jars are completely dry before replacing the lid for storage.
Recovery Diary
Store the diary in the sling bag to keep it protected and dry. Keep away from moisture. If the cover becomes soiled, wipe gently with a barely damp cloth and allow to dry.

General Storage

Keep Nest Carry in a consistent, accessible location when not in use. The sling bag keeps all components together, so the kit is ready to go whenever needed without assembling from different locations.

It requires no guessing about size, no concern about personal preference, and no worry about whether it will actually be used. The completeness of the kit and the thoughtfulness of its assembly make it a gift that communicates genuine care and attention. At ₹ 1,500, it is priced to be accessible while remaining substantial and considered.

For women whose recovery extends over many months, Nest Carry provides a sustained organisational framework. The diary can be supplemented with additional notebooks as needed. The therapy ball continues to support daily hand and arm movement throughout the recovery period. The bag remains useful for as long as recovery essentials need to be carried and organised.
Section 11  —  A Gentle Note

Recovery has a way of generating an endless list of things to manage, track, carry, and remember. Appointments, medications, observations, questions, items to bring, items to collect — the list grows at a time when the energy to manage it is at its lowest.

Nest Carry cannot make recovery simpler than it is. But it can make the practical elements of it a little more organised, a little less scattered, and a little more within reach. One bag. Everything in it. Always in the same place.

The therapy ball is in there for the days when gentle movement is the most useful thing you can do. The diary is in there for the days when writing something down is the only way to keep hold of it. The jars are in there because sometimes recovery is just that practical, and having the right container matters.
You are managing something hard. Let Nest Carry manage a small part of it for you.
Section 12  —  Frequently Asked Questions
What is Nest Carry?

Nest Carry is a complete recovery support kit containing a sling bag, smiley therapy ball, recovery diary, pen, and two collection jars (50 mL and 100 mL). It is designed to keep everyday recovery essentials organised and within reach throughout the course of post-surgical recovery.

Section 02  —  Product Overview

PetalWrap is a premium comfort towel designed to bring genuine softness, considered design, and everyday ease to one of the most routine moments of your day. At 58 or more inches in length and 27 to 28 inches in width, it is a full-size towel with the dimensions to wrap comfortably around the body — offering the kind of generous coverage that a standard-size towel often falls short of.

Made from bamboo plant-fiber fabric, PetalWrap has a soft, naturally breathable quality that distinguishes it from standard cotton towels. The woven herringbone pattern gives the fabric visual texture and structural integrity, and the tassel-finished ends elevate it from a utility item to something that feels genuinely considered and beautiful in a bathroom or recovery space.

PetalWrap is available in four colours — Camellia, Aparajita, Magnolia, and Jade Vine — each produced in the same premium woven fabric. These are not conventional towel colours. They are chosen to feel personal and aesthetically deliberate, making PetalWrap a comfort object that you notice and enjoy rather than simply reach for without thought.

For women recovering from breast surgery, where skin on the chest, underarm, and arm may be sensitive for weeks or months, the softness and gentleness of the fabric is particularly meaningful. But PetalWrap is designed to remain in regular use long after recovery — as an everyday towel that happens to be more considered, more beautiful, and more genuinely comfortable than most.
Section 03  —  Product Story

The name PetalWrap comes from the image of a flower petal — one of nature’s most quietly perfect materials. A petal is soft without being fragile. It is light without being insubstantial. It wraps around what it holds with a gentle completeness that requires no force. And it is, simply and entirely, beautiful.

PetalWrap was designed from that image. Not from the question of what a towel should do — that question has one obvious answer — but from the question of what a towel should feel like. The answer: like something from nature. Like something that is gentle before it is anything else. Like something you are glad to reach for at the end of the day, not just because it is there.

The choice of bamboo plant-fiber fabric follows directly from that intention. Bamboo produces fibers that are softer than standard cotton, more breathable, and naturally gentle in a way that is intrinsic to the material rather than applied through finishing treatments. A towel made from bamboo plant-fiber fabric is doing the same job as any towel, but it is doing it with a different quality of contact. That difference is what PetalWrap is built on.

The dimensions — 58 or more inches in length, 27 to 28 inches wide — come from a similar conviction. A towel that is too small to wrap around the body, that leaves parts of you uncovered or forces uncomfortable positions to make it work, is not a comfort object. It is a compromise. PetalWrap is sized to wrap generously, to cover completely, and to make the simple act of drying off after a shower or bath feel like something unhurried and comfortable.

The tassel-finished ends are a detail that could have been omitted. They are not structural. They do not affect the towel’s performance. But they change how the towel looks and how it feels to own it — the difference between a towel that is adequate and one that is genuinely lovely. Recovery deserves lovely. Everyday life deserves lovely.
Inspired by the softness of nature. Designed for the softness of yours.
Section 04  —  What Makes It Special
Bamboo Plant-Fiber Fabric

The core material of PetalWrap is bamboo plant-fiber fabric. Bamboo fiber is measurably softer than standard cotton at equivalent fabric weights, with a smoother surface texture that is gentler against the skin. It is also naturally breathable and moisture-absorbent, which are the qualities that matter most in a towel. This material is not a premium additive to the design — it is the foundation of it.
Generous Full-Size Dimensions

PetalWrap measures 58 or more inches in length and 27 to 28 inches in width. These dimensions allow the towel to wrap fully around the body with coverage to spare. For women who have had chest or underarm surgery and may need to dry themselves carefully and gently, the extra size means less manoeuvring, less repositioning, and less contact with sensitive areas than a smaller towel requires.
Woven Herringbone Pattern

The herringbone weave is not purely decorative. The woven structure gives the fabric a dimensional surface that is more effective at absorbing moisture and more resilient through repeated washing than plain-weave alternatives. The pattern also gives each colour visual depth — the way light moves across the angled weave brings the colour to life rather than presenting it as flat. The result is a towel that looks as premium as it feels.
Tassel-Finished Ends

The hand-knotted tassel fringe at both ends of PetalWrap is the detail that distinguishes it from a functional towel and makes it a considered object. The tassels are finished in matching thread to the body of the towel, creating a cohesive look that works as a beach towel, a bath towel, a wrap after yoga, or a beautiful addition to a bathroom. They are also a signal: this towel was made with attention to the full experience of owning it.
Four Distinct, Named Colours

Camellia, Aparajita, Magnolia, and Jade Vine are not generic colour options. Each has a name, a character, and a relationship to a specific part of the natural world. They offer a genuine choice — a colour that reflects something about the person who chooses it — rather than a range of neutral towel tones designed to offend no one.
Gentle Against Sensitive Post-Surgical Skin

The chest, underarm, and arm areas following breast surgery can remain sensitive for weeks or months after the procedure. The softness of bamboo plant-fiber fabric and the smooth surface of the herringbone weave make PetalWrap gentler against these areas than standard cotton towels, reducing friction and irritation during the daily routine of bathing and drying.
A Towel That Works Beyond Recovery

PetalWrap is designed for the recovery period but not limited to it. As an everyday towel, it performs with the same quality that makes it useful during recovery — soft, absorbent, generous in size, and beautiful enough to enjoy. It is a product designed to remain in regular use indefinitely, not to be set aside once healing is complete.
Section 05  —  Key Benefits
Softness That Is Felt Immediately

The difference between a bamboo plant-fiber towel and a standard cotton towel is apparent from the first touch. The surface is smoother, the texture more even, and the contact against skin noticeably gentler. For everyday use, this is a quality-of-life improvement. For women in recovery whose skin may be sensitive or reactive in specific areas, it is a meaningful practical benefit that reduces the discomfort of an otherwise ordinary daily task.
Generous Size That Covers Fully

At 58 or more inches long and 27 to 28 inches wide, PetalWrap is among the more generously sized towels available at its price point. This size is not incidental. A towel that wraps completely around the body without adjustment or repositioning makes the process of drying after bathing simpler, more comfortable, and less demanding of the arm movement that may be restricted or uncomfortable during recovery. For everyday use outside of recovery, the full coverage of a larger towel is simply a better experience.
Absorbency That Performs

The bamboo plant-fiber fabric and the herringbone weave together produce a towel that absorbs moisture effectively without leaving skin feeling incompletely dried. The woven structure draws moisture away from the skin surface, and the natural properties of bamboo fiber mean the towel dries more quickly after use than denser synthetic alternatives. This reduces the buildup of bacteria and odour that comes with towels that stay damp for extended periods.
A Beautiful Object in a Recovery Space

Recovery spaces — the bathroom, the bedroom, the areas of the home given over to healing — tend to accumulate clinical objects: medical supplies, medications, equipment. PetalWrap is a deliberate counter to that tendency. A towel in Camellia or Jade Vine hanging in the bathroom is a beautiful object that adds warmth and colour to a space that can otherwise feel functional and austere. The tassels, the woven pattern, the richness of the four colours — these details matter in the context of daily life during recovery.
Colour That Feels Personal

Choosing which PetalWrap to order is a small but genuine act of self-expression. The four colour options are different enough to represent distinct preferences: the warmth of Camellia, the confidence of Aparajita, the softness of Magnolia, the freshness of Jade Vine. Owning a towel in a colour you love is not vanity. It is the kind of small, daily pleasure that contributes to feeling like yourself during a period when many things feel outside your control.
Easy to Care For

PetalWrap is designed for regular use and regular washing. Bamboo plant-fiber fabric maintains its softness and absorbency through repeated washing cycles at the recommended temperature without significant degradation over time. The tassel ends are finished to prevent fraying during normal laundry use. PetalWrap is not a delicate item that requires special handling — it is a premium everyday towel that holds its quality through practical daily life.
Section 06  —  Materials & Construction
Bamboo Plant-Fiber Fabric

PetalWrap is made from bamboo plant-fiber fabric. Bamboo fiber is derived from the bamboo plant through a process that produces a soft, fine, natural textile. The fibers are finer than standard cotton fibers, which results in a smoother surface texture and noticeably softer feel against the skin.

Bamboo fabric is also naturally moisture-wicking and breathable, which are the qualities that govern how effectively a towel absorbs water and how quickly it dries after use. The moisture-absorption quality means the towel draws water from the skin efficiently; the breathability means it releases that moisture into the air rather than holding it against the fabric, which keeps the towel feeling fresher between washes and helps it dry more quickly after use.

The colour in bamboo plant-fiber fabric is more vibrant and deeper than in equivalent cotton fabrics because of the smoothness of the fiber surface. This is why the four colours of PetalWrap — Camellia, Aparajita, Magnolia, and Jade Vine — appear rich and consistent rather than washed-out or uneven.
Herringbone Weave Construction

The woven structure of PetalWrap is a herringbone pattern, visible as a series of diagonal angled lines across the surface of the fabric. This weave has been used in premium textiles for centuries because of its combination of structural strength, visual elegance, and practical absorbency.

The herringbone structure creates a dimensional surface with more contact points per square inch than a plain weave. Section 09  —  How To Use
Application
Clean and dry the brow area completely before application. Ensure no moisturiser, oil, or makeup residue remains on the skin, as this will reduce adhesion.

Hold the brow above your brow bone in the mirror and identify your preferred position before applying. This step prevents misplacement and allows adjustment before the brow is in contact with the skin.
Apply following the instructions included in the guide. Position from the inner corner outward, pressing gently along the full length of the brow to ensure even contact with the skin.
Hold gently for a few seconds and check the position in the mirror. Minor adjustments may be possible immediately after application before the adhesion fully sets.
Repeat for the second brow, using the first as a reference point for height and position symmetry.
During the Day

BrowBloom is designed for all-day wear through a normal daily routine. Avoid heavy rubbing or pressing on the brow area. If the brows come into contact with water, pat gently rather than rubbing to dry.
Removal

Remove BrowBloom gently at the end of the day. Begin at the inner corner of the brow and lift carefully toward the outer corner. Do not pull quickly or forcefully, which can damage the brow and the skin. If there is resistance, a small amount of gentle oil or makeup remover applied at the edge will help release the adhesion without force.
After Removal
Clean the brow gently to remove any residue and allow it to dry completely before storing. Store flat in the included guide or a clean, dry surface away from dust and heat.

Section 08  —  How To Use
Preparation
Use the cuticle stick to gently push back cuticles.
Lightly file the surface of each natural nail to remove shine. This improves adhesion significantly.

Size Selection

Before applying adhesive, hold each press-on nail against the corresponding finger to identify the best size. The nail should cover the full width of the nail bed without extending beyond the edges. If between sizes, the smaller size is generally preferable as it will sit more naturally.
Application
Apply a small amount of adhesive to the back of the press-on nail.
Place the nail at the base of the natural nail, just above the cuticle line.
Press firmly and hold for five to ten seconds.
Work from the little finger to the thumb on one hand, then repeat on the other.

Soak fingertips in warm water for five to ten minutes to soften the adhesive. Gently lift the edge of the nail from the sides and ease it away from the natural nail. Do not pull or force. If resistance remains, soak for longer before attempting again.

Clean any adhesive residue from the press-on nail gently, allow to dry, and store in the pouch for reuse.

The face in the mirror is the same face, but something at the crown is different, and that difference carries.

The sense of moving through the world in a way that feels like yourself. The ability to walk into a room and be focused on what is happening in the room rather than on what is happening on your head.

Together, BloomCrown represents exactly what it is: a collection of wigs designed to bring together comfort, natural appearance, and the kind of everyday confidence that comes from feeling like yourself at the crown of your head — the place from which the whole of how you present yourself to the world begins.

If you have remaining hair, smooth it down with a wig cap if preferred, to create an even surface beneath the wig.
Hold the wig at the front and position the front hairline of the wig at your natural hairline position.
Lower the wig from front to back until the cap is fully seated on the head.

Style as desired.

Storage

Do not sleep in the wig
Do not swim in the wig
Do not store compressed or folded

How long will it last?
With proper daily care — detangling after each wear, storing on a stand, washing correctly, and avoiding excessive heat — a BloomCrown wig is designed to last many months of daily wear.
Do I need a wig stand?
Yes. A wig stand is included with BloomCrown. Storing the wig on a stand when not in use is the single most important thing you can do to preserve the style and the shape of the cap over time.
Can I sleep in it?
No. Remove the wig before sleeping. Sleeping in a wig causes tangling and significantly reduces its lifespan.
Is it suitable for permanent hair loss?
Yes. BloomCrown is appropriate for both temporary treatment-related hair loss and permanent or long-term hair loss from any cause.
